assessment: The incumbent provides a repeatable conversational routine and printed access: seven frequent attendees value its structure (H3-O6), and nine regularly rely on print (H3-O7). Predictability reducing entry and coordination effort is a plausible account, not an established cause. Its concrete limitation is that five occasional attendees struggled to enter conversations already familiar to partners (H3-O6); the same continuity may benefit regulars while requiring an entry bridge for others. Pair delays and changes (H3-O5) do not establish proficiency mismatch. Only 49 of 72 slips report the speaking target and 48 identify preparation; missing slips, untimed speech and unlinked weeks prevent an all-attendee success estimate. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Retaining the routine while testing narrow changes is warranted.

openings.claim: Explicit session dates and one clearly marked next preparation task on each printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier tasks.
openings.delta: Retain the weekly topic and optional message, but add a reusable dated preparation box, available at each session regardless of previous attendance.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline and correct next-task identification rises; blank answers may persist if access or comprehension dominates.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, count correct, earlier and blank preparation answers against total attendance; separately log printing and clarification minutes. Seek 85% correct with total coordination below 90 minutes weekly.
assumptions: Volunteers can specify the next task before printing.
Printed information remains obtainable without an account or smartphone.

openings.claim: A shared fresh opening prompt with a brief reciprocal introduction may help occasional attendees enter conversations without discarding the familiar session structure.
openings.delta: Replace the first pair prompt with a self-contained exchange requiring no previous-session knowledge; partners choose follow-up complexity without public proficiency labels.
openings.prediction: Early partner changes and reported entry difficulty decrease, especially among occasional attendees; unchanged pair-formation delays would locate a separate bottleneck.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and fresh opening prompts across six sessions. Observe formation delay and early changes; ask anonymous attendance-frequency, entry-difficulty and useful-speaking questions. Record coordination time and preserve the 75-minute session.
assumptions: Fresh prompts can be drawn from existing sheets.
Changing attendance composition limits causal interpretation.
